To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the CCR and OEF in patients with major CAAO were significantly reduced, and the OEF in patients who had a CCR of less than 2.5 mL/100 g per min was higher than that in patients who had an OEF of less than 50%.
the CBF and CBV in patients with severe MCAO were significantly decreased compared with those of controls.
cerebral oxygen metabolism and blood flow were reduced in patients with MCAO, and cerebral circulatory reserve capacity was reduced in patients with severe MCAO.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between cerebral circulatory and metabolic reserve and the severity of major cerebral artery occlusion.
the relationship between cerebral circulatory capacity and oxygen utilization in patients with major carotid or vertebrobasilar occlusive disease, using PET.
the relationship between cerebral oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral circulatory reserve capacity (CCRC), and cerebral blood flow (CBF) in patients with major cerebrovascular disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of the oxygen extraction fraction as an indicator of the adequacy of cerebral oxygen delivery in patients with cerebral ischemia is still not well established.
the use of the CCR in patients with MCAO disease is not justified.
the relationship between cerebral oxygen extraction fraction and circulatory reserve is not linear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cerebral circulatory reserve is a major determinant of oxygen extraction fraction in cerebral ischemia.
the brain is able to maintain a normal oxygen extraction fraction (OEF) despite a reduced cerebral blood flow (CBF) reserve in patients with major carotid artery occlusion.
the cerebral circulation is able to increase its oxygen delivery capacity in response to an increase in cerebral oxygen consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between CCR and OEF is not a constant.
the brain's ability to increase its blood flow is related to how much of the blood is used to produce energy.
